To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the failure rate of BGA components is strongly dependent on thermal cycling parameters, especially ΔT and lower dwell temperature, and that failure modes differ significantly depending on the thermal cycling profile.
the characteristic lifetime is strongly influenced by the temperature difference (Δ T), the lower dwell temperature, the lower dwell time, the mean temperature, and the ramp rate.
the failure mechanisms are different in the three lifetime group categories and the failure mechanisms in the first group are not the same as those in the other two groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of thermal-cycling test parameters on the reliability of BGA solder interconnections, and with the failure mechanisms that are responsible for the observed lifetime differences.
identifying the effects of various thermal cycling parameters on the lifetime and failure mechanisms of BGA component boards.
the effects of thermal cycle test parameters on the reliability of solder interconnections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thermal cycling test parameters affect the lifetime of the solder interconnection.
the thermal cycling parameters affect the lifetime of BGA solder interconnections.
the highly accelerated conditions produce failure mechanisms different from the ones in the mildly/nonaccelerating conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermal cycling test parameters can be used to accelerate the failure process.
thermal cycling conditions should be chosen to be representative of real-use conditions.
the thermal cycling parameters have to be selected with great care to avoid accelerated failure mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
one should not rely on accelerated test results without a thorough understanding of the failure mechanisms and their correlation with field failure mechanisms.
thermal cycling profiles with ΔT of 10–15°C, mean temperature of 60–65°C, dwell time of 5–15 min, and ramp rate of 1–2°C/s are the most efficient in terms of lifetime statistics.
thermal cycling conditions that produce a large number of failures in a reasonable amount of time should be avoided.
